title: Element distinctness and k-distinctness

problem.name: Element distinctness and k-distinctness
problem.statement_latex:
\textbf{Element distinctness.} Given $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in[M]$, decide whether $x_i=x_j$ for some $i\ne j$. The input is accessed by coherent indexed queries; collision detection is a primitive for data processing.

\textbf{$k$-distinctness.} Given $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in[M]$ and fixed $k\ge3$, decide whether some value occurs at least $k$ times. Complexity counts indexed input queries.

quantum.headline_latex: \textbf{Element distinctness.} $\Theta(n^{2/3})$ queries by the Ambainis Johnson-graph quantum walk, with $\widetilde O(n^{2/3})$ time when the walk data structure supports coherent updates.
quantum.details_latex: \textbf{$k$-distinctness.} $O(n^{1-2^{k-2}/(2^k-1)})$ queries by Belovs' learning graph; the bound is for constant $k$.
